title: Two sum with a seen-map
prompt: Implement twoSum(nums []int, target int) []int returning the two indices whose values add to target. Exactly one answer exists. One pass, O(n).
explanation: Store value -> index as you go and look for the complement before inserting. Checking first is what stops an element pairing with itself, and it means you never need a second pass.
hints: One map, filled as you go. What do you look up before you insert?
For nums[i] you want target-nums[i]. Store value -> index.

title: Lower bound with half-open bounds
prompt: Implement lowerBound(nums []int, target int) int on a sorted slice: the index of the first element >= target, or len(nums) if there is none. No use of the sort package.
explanation: Half-open [lo, hi) with hi starting at len(nums) is what lets the answer be len(nums) without a special case. The invariant is that everything below lo is < target and everything from hi up is >= target, so lo is the answer when they meet.
hints: Search the half-open range [0, len(nums)]; the answer can be len(nums).
Keep the invariant: everything left of lo is < target, everything at hi or beyond is >= target.
refs: LC 34 Find First and Last Position

title: Two pointers that skip junk
prompt: Implement isPalindrome(s string) bool, considering only letters and digits and ignoring case. Two pointers, O(1) extra space (no cleaned copy of the string).
explanation: The skip loops need the i < j guard too, otherwise an all-punctuation string walks a pointer off the end. Comparing in place beats building a filtered copy: same time, no allocation.
hints: Two indices walking inward, skipping anything that is not alphanumeric.
Advance each pointer past junk in its own inner loop, and guard i < j inside those loops too.
